_comment: Verified live against the Pliny gateway 2026-09-20. selfHosted context = measured max_model_len reported by the gateway itself, NOT hand-entered. hosted context / max_output = the limits listed on the Pliny Model Catalog page (2026-09-25); hosted entries without them fall back to 200k / 64k in code. tool_call = a real tool_calls response was observed.
_thinkingNote: selfHosted `thinking` = measured by `apps/vscode/scripts/probe-pliny-free-models.ts --thinking` on 2026-09-24 (see docs/pliny-free-auto-thinking.md): whether the model reasons with no hint (defaultOn), and which request field reliably turns reasoning off (off) or on (on). Never hand-guess these: an unsupported field such as reasoning_effort is rejected with a 400 by several backends.
_pricingNote: pricing is USD per 1M tokens, mapped straight into ModelInfo.pricing. selfHosted models are always free (pricing: 0/0/0/0, and Pliny does not count them against the monthly budget), stamped in code (see toModelInfo), not here. hosted prices marked `PLINY_CATALOG` in `priceSource` are copied from the Pliny Model Catalog page (docs site, 'Model Catalog', read 2026-09-25); where a model has both a Standard and an Azure price the Azure one is used, because that is the deployment Pliny serves. `PUBLIC_ESTIMATE` entries are the public list price of the closest known model, standing in for a price the Pliny page does not list. hosted entries with NO `pricing` block (gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-5.6-luna, Kimi-K2.7-Code, gemini-3.7-flash, google-vertex/glm-5.2) are not on the Pliny page and have no confident stand-in, so they are left unpriced on purpose and render as 'price unknown'. Never guess a number here.
_paramsNote: `params` = parameter counts in billions from the model's public card (`total` = all weights, `active` = weights used per token; equal for a dense model). Closed models (Claude, GPT, Gemini) do not publish them and have no `params`. `name` / `summary` are the picker's display name and its one- or two-sentence strengths/weaknesses blurb; keep summaries qualitative so they do not go stale.

selfHosted.name: GLM-5.2
selfHosted.summary: The strongest free open-weight model for coding and long agentic runs, with the largest context. This pool is the slowest replica; the vmodels pool serves the same model faster.

selfHosted.name: GLM-5.2 (internal tests)
selfHosted.summary: GLM-5.2 on the internal-tests pool: top free model for coding and huge contexts. A test deployment, so availability can change without notice.

selfHosted.name: GLM-5.2 (vmodels)
selfHosted.summary: GLM-5.2 on the load-balanced pool: the best free choice for large codebases and long tasks. Thinks by default, so simple replies are slower than on smaller models.

selfHosted.note: reasons inside content; no measured off-switch
selfHosted.name: Kimi K2.6
selfHosted.summary: Fast, strong agentic coder and reliable tool caller; FreeAuto's workhorse. Reasons inside the answer text and cannot be told to stop thinking.

selfHosted.name: Nemotron 3 Super
selfHosted.summary: Efficient hybrid Mamba MoE: a quick, dependable all-rounder for everyday agent work. Less capable than GLM-5.2 or Kimi on hard coding problems.

selfHosted.name: Qwen3.8 27B
selfHosted.summary: Recent dense 27B model that codes well for its size, with a 256K context. Slow to generate on this pool, and weaker than the big MoE models on complex tasks.

selfHosted.name: Qwen3.6 27B
selfHosted.summary: Dense 27B model with good coding for its size and a 256K context. Slow first token on this pool; superseded by Qwen3.8 27B.

selfHosted.name: Qwen3.8 27B (SIA)
selfHosted.summary: Qwen3.8 27B on the SIA pool: same model and context as the main pool. This pool was down in the last probe, so expect failovers.

selfHosted.name: Gemma 4 31B (reasoning)
selfHosted.summary: Google's dense 31B with switchable reasoning and a 256K context: solid, balanced general model. Not as strong at coding as the Qwen or GLM models.

selfHosted.name: Qwen3.5 397B
selfHosted.summary: Large MoE with strong reasoning and coding, and a 220K context. Generation is fairly slow, and the newer Qwen3.6/3.8 dense models now match it on coding.

selfHosted.name: Qwen3.5 397B (SIA)
selfHosted.summary: Qwen3.5 397B on the SIA pool. Reasons inside the answer text, and the pool was down in the last probe.

selfHosted.name: Nemotron 3 Ultra
selfHosted.summary: NVIDIA's largest open reasoning model, quick for its size and good at planning and multi-step reasoning. Reasons inside the answer text, which clutters replies.

selfHosted.name: Llama 3.3 70B (NIM)
selfHosted.summary: Older dense model that answers quickly and calls tools reliably, without reasoning. Clearly weaker than current models at coding and long tasks.

selfHosted.name: Qwen3 Coder 480B
selfHosted.summary: Coding-specialised MoE that is good at edits and tool use, with no thinking overhead. Slow generation on this pool and only 128K context.

selfHosted.name: Qwen3.6 27B (fine-tuned)
selfHosted.summary: Synopsys fine-tune of Qwen3.6 27B. The slowest free model in probes, with half the base model's context.

selfHosted.name: Qwen3.6 35B-A3B
selfHosted.summary: Very fast small MoE, good for quick questions. Only 3B active parameters, reasons inside the answer text, and often skips tool calls.

selfHosted.name: Gemma 4 31B
selfHosted.summary: Google's dense 31B without reasoning: steady, balanced general model. Reasoning cannot be switched on through the gateway, and coding trails the Qwen and GLM models.

selfHosted.name: Llama 3.3 70B
selfHosted.summary: Older dense model that answers quickly and calls tools reliably, without reasoning. Clearly weaker than current models at coding and long tasks.

selfHosted.name: Llama 3.3 70B (74K)
selfHosted.summary: Llama 3.3 70B on a smaller-context pool: dependable tool calls, no reasoning. Weaker than current models, and the 74K context fills quickly.

selfHosted.name: Qwen2.5 32B
selfHosted.summary: Older dense model that is fine for short, simple tasks. Weak at agentic coding by current standards, with a 64K context.

selfHosted.name: Qwen3 Next 80B-A3B
selfHosted.summary: Sparse MoE with quick first tokens, suited to short questions. Only 3B active parameters and a 32K context.

selfHosted.name: Llama 3.1 70B
selfHosted.summary: The oldest model in the pool, with dependable tool calls. Slow, a 32K context, and weak at coding by current standards.

hosted.note: strongest coder; supports explicit prompt caching (10x saving)
hosted.priceSource: PUBLIC_ESTIMATE: Anthropic Claude Sonnet public list price (AWS Bedrock); not listed on the Pliny Model Catalog page
hosted.name: Claude Sonnet 5
hosted.summary: The strongest coder available: best at large refactors, debugging and long agentic runs, with image input and prompt caching. A paid model that counts against your Pliny budget.

hosted.name: Claude Sonnet 4.6
hosted.summary: Excellent coder with a 1M-token context, image input and prompt caching. Slightly behind Sonnet 5 at the same price.

hosted.priceSource: PLINY_CATALOG 2026-09-25 (input/output); cache prices are the Anthropic public list price, the page lists none
hosted.name: Claude Sonnet 4.5
hosted.summary: Previous-generation Sonnet, still a strong coder with image input. Same price as the newer Sonnets for less capability.

hosted.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
hosted.summary: Fast, cheap Claude, good for simple edits, questions and sub-agents. Noticeably weaker than Sonnet on hard reasoning and large changes.

hosted.priceSource: PUBLIC_ESTIMATE: priced as Claude Sonnet 4.6, the preset's base model; the preset is not listed on the Pliny Model Catalog page
hosted.name: Claude Sonnet 4.6 (high thinking)
hosted.summary: Sonnet 4.6 with a large thinking budget preset: best for planning, design and tricky debugging. Slower and costlier per turn (thinking is billed as output), and no image input.

hosted.priceSource: PUBLIC_ESTIMATE: priced as Claude Sonnet 4.6, the preset's base model; the preset is not listed on the Pliny Model Catalog page
hosted.name: Claude Sonnet 4.6 (medium thinking)
hosted.summary: Sonnet 4.6 with a medium thinking budget: a balance of reasoning depth and speed. No image input.

hosted._contextNote: The Pliny page lists 400K, but that window includes the 128K output. 241K-token prompts are accepted live (2026-09-25); a 340K one is rejected with 429 on every retry (it exceeds the deployment's per-minute token quota). So PlinyCode budgets the 272K input share.
hosted.name: GPT-5.2
hosted.summary: Strong reasoning and planning with a large context, image input and automatic caching. Can be slow while it reasons, and its reasoning effort cannot be tuned from PlinyCode.

hosted.name: GPT-5.6 Terra
hosted.summary: An Azure OpenAI GPT-5.6 deployment. Not yet characterised in PlinyCode; its price and limits are not on the Pliny catalog page.

hosted.name: GPT-5.6 Luna
hosted.summary: An Azure OpenAI GPT-5.6 deployment. Not yet characterised in PlinyCode; its price and limits are not on the Pliny catalog page.

hosted.name: Kimi K2.6 (Azure)
hosted.summary: Kimi K2.6 hosted on Azure: a strong agentic coder at a low price. The same model is free self-hosted, so pick this only when that pool is busy.

hosted.name: Kimi K2 Thinking
hosted.summary: Kimi's long-reasoning model: good at multi-step problems, and cheap. Slow, verbose thinking, and older than K2.6.

hosted.name: Kimi K2.7 Code
hosted.summary: Kimi's coding-specialised release, on an internal-tests pool. Price not on the Pliny catalog page, and availability may change.

hosted.name: Gemini 3.7 Flash
hosted.summary: Google's newest fast Flash model. Not yet characterised in PlinyCode; its price and limits are not on the Pliny catalog page.

hosted.name: Gemini 3.5 Flash
hosted.summary: Fast model with a 1M-token context, good for reading large codebases or logs. Weaker than Claude or GPT-5.2 at careful multi-file edits.

hosted.name: Gemini 2.5 Flash
hosted.summary: The cheapest paid model, with a 1M-token context, fine for summaries and simple tasks. Older, and weak at agentic coding.

hosted.name: GLM-5.2 (Vertex)
hosted.summary: GLM-5.2 hosted on Google Vertex. The same model is free self-hosted with a larger context, and this deployment's price is not on the Pliny catalog page.

hosted.priceSource: PLINY_CATALOG 2026-09-25 (cache read listed as ~$0.10 to ~$0.12; the upper bound is used)
hosted.name: GLM-5 (Vertex)
hosted.summary: Previous-generation GLM, a capable open-weight coder at a low price. The newer GLM-5.2 is free self-hosted and stronger.
